newsitem.title: USA: Medical Graphics sees Q4 loss after charge.
newsitem.headline: Medical Graphics sees Q4 loss after charge.

text.p: Medical Graphics Corp, a manufacturer of cardiorespiratory technology, said Wednesday it expects to report a loss approaching $2.00 per share in the fourth quarter, despite increases in revenues and gross profit.
The loss includes the impact of a one-time charge that the company will take in the quarter, in addition to a loss from operations of $0.70 to $0.80 per share.
The company said the one-time charge will be close to $3 million. Included is a charge for the restructuring of its international business to eliminate unprofitable operations.
Additionally, provisions are being made to recognize tax liabilities related to service revenues and to more appropriately value inventories and customer receivables, Medical Graphics said.
The company said the operating loss stems from significant increases in operating expenses compared to one year ago, mostly in selling and research and development spending.

The increase in selling expenses reflects the company's efforts to increase sales by enhancing its marketing and product education programs. Medical Graphics said it also spent more money on research and development to upgrade product software. Additionally, general and administrative costs were higher due to a management restructuring.
Medical Graphics makes non-invasive coardiorespiratory diagnostic systems for the treatment of heart and lung diseases.
Its stock closed up 3/4 Wednesday at 5-3/8.
